text.p: By Peter Campbell*
AUSTRALIA DAY AFLOAT AND AWASH

Despite the constant rain on Australia Day, large fleets still turned out for the 161st Australia Day Regatta on Sydney Harbour and for the record number of satellite Australia Day regattas on waterways throughout the metropolitan area and as far north as Lake Macquarie.

Offshore, more than 50 yachts set sail in the race from Sydney Harbour to Botany Bay and return for the City of Sydney Sesquicentenary Trophy, a race which took the leaders more than five hours to complete.

Line honours went to Capital Investments chairman CHARLES CURRAN with his new IAIN MURRAY-designed 60-footer Sydney, just two minutes ahead of the 50-footer Wild Thing (BOB ELLIS). On corrected time, the International Measurement System (IMS) winner was ROGER HICKMAN's 43-footer Atara.

On the harbour, victory in Division 1 went to Styx, owned by well-known businessman and fund-raiser extraordinaire GEOFF LEE, an appropriate win as he is a member of the Australia Day Regatta management committee.
CURRAN is also closely involved in the regatta planning as a member of its advisory council.
The other major trophy winner was the appropriately-named (for the day) 18-footer Dark and Stormy, skippered by sailing commentator MICHAEL SPIES.
Among the many satellite regattas was the one at Manly Yacht Club (MYC), which hosted the Southmark for the Olympic Soling class, the only keelboat class for the 2000 Olympic Games.
Local interest is building up in the three-crew Solings and the series even drew an entry from Western Australia skippered by a Russian yachtsman, EDGAR VITTE.

He and his crew, BRETT RIDDLE and DAMON NEAVES, sailing Tower Life, provided plenty of competition for the ultimate winner, Sydney Gold, skippered by sailmaker and luckless near-Olympian GARY GIETZ and his crew of ANDREW CUTLER and STEWART DART.
Sydney Gold also won the Australia Day Regatta trophy while the handicap winner was MYC member and Soling enthusiast IVANA McALPINE, with STEVEN O'DRISCOLL and GREG EBELLING in the crew.
WOMEN ON WATER SET FOR RECORD REGATTA

The 1997 WOW Nortel Asia Pacific Women's Regatta on Sydney Harbour from February 9-14 is shaping up as the largest in the event's six-year history and will again be hosted by the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron in conjunction with Women on Water (WOW).
This year's regatta will run over six days, starting with two days of coaching clinics conducted by the ISAF Nations Cup winning skipper Susan Walters.

Then will follow four days of intensive racing in the International J-24 and Elliott 5.9 classes. The Eliott 5.9 will be the junior class, encouraging yachtswomen under 25 years of age. The J-24s will be sailed by a crew of six and the Elliotts by a crew of three.

KERRY GOUDGE, WOW president and an experienced ocean racing sailor, expects a record fleet this year -- probably as many as 120 sailors -- from Tasmania, Victoria, Queensland and New South Wales, with an impressive international contingent so far of four crews from New Zealand.
WOW has a membership of some 600 women Australia-wide, which aims to improve female participation and opportunities within the sport of yachting.
INTERNATIONAL REGATTA PLANNED FOR FIJI
Fiji will host a new international yachting series in the first week of July this year, with yachts from around the world expected to take part.

Fiji yachting and tourism identity DICK SMITH, of Musket Cove Resort, is heading an organising committee of representatives of the Fiji Yachting Association, Lautoka, Musket Cove, Royal Suva and Denarau Island Resort Yacht Clubs, Vuda Point Marina and the Fiji Visitors Bureau.

The series will coincide with the arrival in Fiji of the Expo '98 Round-the-World Rally and the Auckland-to-Denarau race fleets. The international series will comprise five races under the management of the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron.
Yacht owners interested in the series can contact Dick Smith at Musket Cove Resort, Fiji on +679 662215 or fax +679 662633, while information is also available from the Fiji Tourist Bureau in Sydney.
JEWEL IN THE CROWN FOR FARREN-PRICE

Well-known Sydney jeweller and longtime yachting supporter JULIAN FARREN-PRICE appears to have developed a passion for the Northshore-38 cruiser/racer class and has organised a state championship regatta for the weekend of April 19-20.
He is confident between 15 and 20 boats from various ports on the east coast will compete in a four-race series.

The Northshore-38 still rates as one of the best compromise cruiser/racers on the market and excellent value to boot. Among the events they have done well in are the 1995 Pittwater-Coffs Harbour race (1st on PHS), 1996 Gosford to Lord Howe Island race (2nd on PHS) and the SOR Division 1, Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron (1st in 1994 and 1996).

According to Julian, one of the best features of the Northshore-38s are their easily-controlled running and reaching. Given the right wind and sea, the boat will track beautifully, surfing waves at 15-plus knots, he said.
For information on the state championship or Northshore-38 ownership (very unbiased, of course), give Julian a call on 9363-2528.
OCEAN RACING BACK INTO FULL SWING

With all yachts back to their home ports after the Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart (with the exception of the unfortunate Bit'o Fluff, abandoned after losing her keel and turning turtle off Ulladulla), club offshore racing is back into full swing.

The Cruising Yacht Club's pointscore resumed on Australia Day with the City of Sydney Sesquicentenary Trophy race from Sydney to Botany Bay and back. The club will also host the annual races to and from Wollongong for the Tradewinds Trophy over the weekend of February 14-16.
On the same weekend a big fleet will head off from Adelaide in the Fosters' 22nd race to Port Lincoln, followed by Lincoln Week.

The 1996-97 season ends with Middle Harbour Yacht Club's 33rd annual race to Mooloolaba on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, starting on March 22, followed by the Brisbane-to-Gladstone race on Good Friday, March 28.
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
